reply:
Based on this single image, it is not possible to definitively determine if omentum is present.

The image shows a large, irregular, nodular, and hemorrhagic mass. Typical omentum appears as a lacy, fatty apron of tissue, which is not clearly visible here.

However, in some medical conditions, the omentum can be heavily infiltrated by a tumor, creating a firm mass (sometimes called "omental caking"). Therefore, it is possible that the specimen is an involved omentum, but this cannot be confirmed by visual inspection alone.

A definitive identification of the tissues and a diagnosis of the mass can only be made by a pathologist through a microscopic examination (histopathology) of the specimen. If this is your specimen or that of a patient, you must consult the attending surgeon or pathologist for the official report.
